claims.value: five distinct mammalian bone specimens identified at family level, each split into AmBic and Acid extraction aliquots
claims.evidence: Paper Table 1 lists R10300 as Rhinocerotidae, R10340 and GdC-1 as Ursidae, R10357 as Equidae, and GdC-26 as Bovidae. Family-level taxonomy is retained without assigning a species. The PRIDE protocol describes homogenized powder from each specimen divided into aliquots. Biological replicate IDs 1-5 index distinct specimens and repeat across the two methods.

claims.evidence: The paper method paragraphs separately state that AmBic and Acid extracts were each digested overnight with trypsin. The record also discusses Lys-C and mixed digests for different methods outside this subset.

claims.value: variable oxidation M and P, deamidation N/Q, N-terminal pyro-Glu from Q and E
claims.evidence: The paper MaxQuant methods and PRIDE data-processing protocol list oxidation M, deamidation NQ, Gln to pyro-Glu, Glu to pyro-Glu and proline hydroxylation as variable search modifications. Oxidation P represents proline hydroxylation.

limitations: This ten-run SDRF covers only specimens with prior family-level taxonomic identifications under two single-enzyme extraction methods. The family names do not assert a species identity. The other 92 accession RAW files remain outside this artifact, six of which are in a separately approved reindeer SDRF.

The publication narrative numbers Acid as method 1 and AmBic as method 2, whereas deposited README, SampletoData.csv and RAW filenames number AmBic as 1 and Acid as 2. This SDRF uses the method names; the run map preserves deposited numeric prefixes.
Project-wide PRIDE protocol mentions Trypsin/Lys-C mix for other extraction methods. The paper explicitly documents trypsin alone for both methods represented here.
Sex and developmental stage of the individual animals are not reported. Precise precursor and fragment search tolerances are not stated for this subset and are omitted.
